speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I wish to dedicate my cut to highlighting three important manpower issues in Singapore to enhance fairness and opportunity for all workers, regardless of the work that they do and their workplaces.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: First, Singaporean Core; second, mature and mid-career workers and Professionals, Managers and Executives (PMEs); third, freelance and self-employed.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I congratulate the good work done by the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP).

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I wish to ask MOM to provide an update on how effective the FCF has been to level the playing field for Singaporean PMEs and remove nationality discrimination in hiring practices.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Many PMEs I have met have shared that they are not unhappy with foreign PMEs who bring in huge businesses and investments in Singapore and have unique international competencies.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Instead, they are unhappy with foreign PMEs doing jobs which Singaporeans can undertake and do.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: At the same time, we want to see further efforts to encourage capability transfer, so that we can develop a Singaporean Core across all levels of hierarchy, from rank and file to top management.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In this area of strengthening the Singaporean Core, I have four suggestions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Second, whether MOM can review the salary ceiling for Employment Pass (EP) applicants to level the playing field for our Singaporean PMEs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This is also in consideration of the rise in median and entry salaries of our local PMEs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Third, to review and better scrutinise the FCF exemption on intra-company transfers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Fourth, whether MOM can push ahead in creating more flexible work-from-home opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The question to ask is: are there tasks or jobs that can be arranged to be performed by Singaporeans who require very flexible work arrangements FWAs), for example, stay-at-home dads or mums, caregivers for parents, those with family members who are ill and so on?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I find this important, particularly with an ageing populace.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This can also be a source of employment for those who are not able to fit into the current model of flexible employment, where work can still be delivered for less time-critical tasks.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: On mid-career and mature PMEs, I highlighted during the Budget Debate on the exacting challenges faced by mid-career and mature workers, especially PMEs, in the area of finding work and staying employable.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I wish to ask MOM for an update, including the take-up figures, retrenchment and data on the various schemes under the Adapt and Grow since it was first launched.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In particular, I wish to ask first on the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) – further subdivided into PCP for new entrants as well as those pre-emptive in-employment PCPs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I also wish to ask how MOM intends to make the PCP an attractive option for PMEs and better manage the dropout rate of PCP candidates.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I wish to ask how CSP has made mid-career PMEs more employed and employable.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In particular, are there avenues to further enhance and expand the CSP scheme so as to help more mid-career PMEs land themselves in suitable quality jobs?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Third, the Jobs Bank, now known as the My Careers Future portal.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How successful has the portal been to connect mid-career PMEs to jobs and minimise situations whereby there are jobs and skills mismatches?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I also wish to ask if further enhancements can be made so that the portal can also leverage big data to better enhance job matching.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: By the same token, anecdotally, I still hear complaints of ageism in the hiring of workers in various workplaces.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Though not rampant, this is and will be a growing challenge as we face the imminent challenges of an ageing workforce, an increasingly mature and older workforce, and as we raise the retirement and re-employment ages.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Job redesign and augmented technology and intelligence are imperatives but will not be the dynamic panacea.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I cannot emphasise the need for us to change mindsets and attitudes towards this segment of workers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Besides the tripartite partners, our people and society as a whole must embrace the changing fabric of the Singaporean workforce so that we can overcome unfortunate stereotyping and mental models.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: On freelancers and self-employed, this group of workers are one big group affected by the current Coronavirus Disease of 2019 (COVID-19) situation.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This is so that they can also have the opportunity to go for skills upgrading and training, while receiving a training allowance.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) stands ready to partner the Government to administer the Surrogate Employer Programme, so that we can better encourage our freelancers and SEPs to come forward for training.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: (In Mandarin):   How to ensure that all workers, including white-collar, blue-collar and freelancers, are treated fairly has always been an area of concern of NTUC.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: As the workforce ages, I encourage everyone to change their mindsets and attitudes towards middle-age and senior workers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Thirdly, the COVID-19 outbreak has greatly impacted a lot of freelancers and SEPs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With technological advances and digital disruptions, businesses need talent as they transform.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mid-career workers are concerned as the nature of work and jobs are changing and they worry that there may not be enough or suitable jobs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Paradoxically, we see a situation where companies are seeking skilled talent and are facing a talent crunch.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mid-career workers who are displaced are finding it harder to find suitable employment.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As we focus on supporting mid-career workers on reskilling for new roles to meet changing business requirements, I want to stress that we should also build upon the experience, expertise and knowledge of mid-career workers, especially PMEs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While digital skills and technology are increasingly required to get work done, technologies, for example, AI and data analytics, do not exist in a vacuum.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In fact, if we examine the roles that are in demand, while many of the roles require the ability to handle technology, they are at the same time more complex and multidisciplinary, requiring business acumen and a wide set of skills from different fields, for example, design, marketing, sales and customer services, and even operational know-how.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: These are quality roles and not low-level entry jobs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While mid-career PMEs will need to learn new skills, especially digital skills, they have the experience, expertise and knowledge.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And organisations should and must tap on this valuable talent base.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While younger talent may be equipped with new skills, be agile in learning, they will need time to acquire multidisciplinary skills and expertise that mid-career workers have built up over their careers.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In coping with today's complex and fast-changing market, businesses will need both young and mid-career workers to transform and will benefit from having a diverse talent pool, creating a work environment that effectively engages a diverse workforce of both young and mid-career workers, and this will be a competitive advantage for businesses.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For companies to upskill their own mid-career employees or to hire mid-career employees effectively, they need to also understand the existing skills that their mid-career employees have and also what their business requires.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will enable better alignment of employment development for the new jobs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I hope that the various skills programmes will take this into account and provide the job pathways and relevancy of the existing and new skills required to help mid-career workers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, mid-career transitions may be one of the most daunting experiences for workers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I will touch on the FCF and career transition schemes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Four years ago, my colleague, Member of Parliament Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap, highlighted that the original FCF needed enforcement measures.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I believe that the Minister is well aware of some employers who treat the FCF as, to quote her, "a paper exercise".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The announcement in January that MOM is enhancing the FCF is welcome.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: However, it seems that in recent years, most of the discrimination cases came to the Ministry's attention through whistleblowing.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is the Ministry going to step up proactive detection of its own?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My second point relates to career transition programmes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: PCPs and CSPs are key planks of the Government's Adapt and Grow initiative to help mid-career transitions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To what extent is success hampered by capacity issues, that is, insufficient job openings, or is matching of jobs to applicants the bigger issue?

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, as Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) like the Singapore Manufacturing Federation (SMF) continue to work with enterprises to reskill and train employees, the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit scheme is a welcome announcement.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: However, a common feedback from employees is that they are hesitant to go for training because when they return to the office, they have to deal with accumulated backlog.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, it is pertinent that organisations need to take a long-term view and to look into reskilling their employees.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: The burden is largely on employers right now to juggle the limited resources, uncertain demand, maintaining the payroll and continue with training efforts.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, does the Ministry have in place plans to encourage and educate employers to put in place more facilitative work arrangements to allow for staff to go for training without worrying that they have a large workload to return to?

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: In the same vein, are there plans to alleviate employer difficulties that arise from employees going for reskilling?

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: How can TACs play a role in this journey?

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, the Government has introduced many tripartite committees and initiatives, such as the Singapore Tripartism Forum (STF), National Wages Council (NWC), TAFEP and Tripartite Committee on Employability of Older Workers.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: Such tripartisan initiatives promote greater awareness for fair and progressive employment practices to employers.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: The good work from their efforts are often brought up during our engagement with members from the business communities.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: However, there will always be some errant employers out there who go against the principles of fair and progressive employment.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: We must be careful that in formulating policies, we do not inevitably place bigger burdens on the majority of employers by putting in place measures aimed at preventing the behaviour of the errant minority.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: In turn, employers should support the targeted moves the Government makes to go after bad behaviour.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: In Budget 2020, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat has introduced many measures under the third thrust of the Transformation and Growth strategy to develop the capabilities of our workers.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: SMF is a firm supporter of lifelong learning for workers to be ready for new challenges and opportunities to progress and grow with enterprises.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: One profession I would like to highlight would be the training and development of human resources (HR) professionals.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
text: With the advent of new technologies and the skillsets required emerging in the workforce, our HR professionals would also need to learn new skills and strategies to nurture and manage this new workforce of the future.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: She also warned that there would be "stronger deterrence for discrimination against Singaporeans when hiring, but also stronger support for employers who are committed to giving our people a fair chance." I support this approach by MOM.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For some years, Singaporeans have complained about companies where most of their colleagues are foreigners and Singaporean employees are in the minority.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: That kind of practice cannot be a right practice.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Businesses operating in Singapore must help create more employment opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Government must send a strong signal to companies which discriminate against Singaporeans and favour foreigners that their employment process is wrong.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Singaporeans must be given fair consideration if they meet the right criteria.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Unfair and discriminatory employment practices affect the harmony among Singaporean residents and cause unfair resentment against foreigners who may be genuinely needed in Singapore, due to their specific skills and expertise.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Notwithstanding the exemption, MOM still requires all employers to consider Singaporeans fairly.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: You said, "This is because open advertising for jobs, such as these, is usually done in a different manner.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Furthermore, such jobs only cover 5% of the local workforce, meaning that the vast majority of jobs would be covered by advertising requirements." I believe FCF has served us well in ensuring that there is a strong Singaporean PME core in the industries.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: With the experience gained over almost six years, I wonder whether this is an opportune time to review the FCF to ensure that a proper balance continues to be struck between giving Singaporeans a fair opportunity to access high-quality jobs and ensuring that Singapore is an attractive place to do business.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, in the current economic landscape, it should not matter that jobs above the salary peg only covers 5% of the local workforce.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What is key is whether Singaporeans are fairly considered for the post in question before a foreigner is considered.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Also, the jobs above the current salary ceiling usually involve senior positions, such as C-suite officers in MNCs or banks.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These are high-quality jobs which suitably qualified Singaporeans would be aspiring for.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Second, without advertising, it will never be clear whether qualified Singaporeans are made aware of such job openings.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Lastly, the quantum of the salary ceiling, which is applicable throughout the workforce, is not representative of the average salaries for senior jobs in certain industries, such as finance and technology.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, I was heartened to learn about stronger measures rolled out by the Ministry in January this year against companies that discriminate against Singaporeans during the hiring process.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would the Ministry provide an update on the results of enforcement measures against errant companies in the last 12 months?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What additional measures has the Ministry implemented in the last year to ensure fair hiring practices and a level playing field for Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Minister share an update on its review of the foreign worker hiring policies and the progress on efforts against other forms of workplace discrimination?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: In 2016, I filed an MOM cut on local talents.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: I said then that one of the challenges faced by small and medium enterprises (SMEs) is finding local talent.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: It is common knowledge that companies need high-quality staff for expansion and survival of business.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Many SMEs want to employ local talent but some locals might find that it is more glamorous to work for MNCs.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Then, I had proposed for our trade associations to work closely with institutes of higher learning (IHLs) to close the gaps in employment.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: We should also build up the image of mastery of skills and trade.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: However, many companies, especially smaller scale ones, find it challenging to hire local talents.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Some of the jobs in those three sectors are simply not attractive to locals.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Long project working hours, sector-specific hazards and remote workplace, such as Tuas and Jurong Island, are not helping.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: I am concerned that the challenging terrain faced by these companies would become even more challenging come 2021 and 2023.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: How can we help these companies to smoothen the transition to lesser S Passes and more locals in the future?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: How are our IHLs training locals to fill those roles?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And this year, I am heartened to see that we have continued building on this very strong foundation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, our goal is to say that this is a very exciting year for our senior workers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: There are at least five key new policies and refinements that benefit our senior workers this year.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: These include the Enhanced Second Employment Credit, the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Transition Offsets, Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and the Part-Time Re-employment Grant as well as the Matched Retirement Saving Schemes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And these are on top of the improvements of the Silver Support Scheme that improves on social assistance for our seniors and HDB's Lease Buy-back that strengthens the retirement adequacy of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This is surely the result of MOM's Working Group for Senior Workers, and MOM's willingness to engage many groups of stakeholders, including the People's Action Party (PAP).SG through two Private Members' Motions on seniors over the past two years.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As such, can MOM provide the House with a comprehensive update on measures to help senior workers stay gainfully employed and improve the quality of their jobs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, the new Senior Employment Credit (SEC) addresses the employability of older workers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: However, the evidence linking employer wage subsidies to increasing employment is not encouraging.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, most of the subsidy is a deadweight loss, a transfer to the employer with no policy effect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: How has retention of older workers and new hiring of older workers improved since the existing SEC was introduced?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: To what extent have these improvements been caused by the existing SEC?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And what targets have been set for the new SEC?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, Budget 2020's Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) is an important policy to address the retirement savings shortfall among lower-income Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: However, academic research suggests that Government subsidies for retirement savings have little to modest effects on actually encouraging people to make voluntary contributions to retirement savings, or, to increase those contributions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Engelhardt and Kumar show that increasing the employer savings match rate for company-sponsored retirement account plans in the US generates little improvement in retirement account participation or savings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: First, the majority of workers, or 85%, are passive savers who do not respond to government policies to encourage savings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, the remaining 15%, largely just shift money from their private savings accounts, to their tax-subsidised savings account.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Although this is much better than the 3% of subjects who contributed without any match, the experimental context is important.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Subjects were deciding how to use their US tax refunds and were not contributing out of pocket.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I have previously argued this means we should move away from Government subsidies for voluntary saving, such as our Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS) and CPF tax deduction policies, in favour of Government matching contributions for all mandatory CPF savings, or to all citizens in general.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Nonetheless, how we implement Budget 2020's MRSS could be more important than the dollar amount itself in encouraging retirement savings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Behavioural economics research suggests people fail to save for retirement due to a combination of loss aversion and procrastination.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: To address loss aversion, we can ask people to contribute out of future income, rather than out of pocket.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: To address procrastination, we can ask people to make a commitment to contribute, which becomes a passive action in the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This avoids needing to make an active choice each time a contribution is due.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These behavioural principles are summarised by Benartzi and Thaler as "Save More Tomorrow".

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: To improve the take-up of MRSS, we could ask eligible Singaporeans to commit to contribute part or all of their future Government payouts to their CPF account.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Such payouts could include the GST Voucher-Cash, the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) cash payout and one-off payments, such as the Care and Support–Cash payout.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We can also ask employers whether workers can commit to contribute part of future work income, such as the Additional Wage Supplement, annual bonuses and annual wage increments, to their CPF account for the savings match.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Such commitments must be revocable any time before the CPF contribution is made, in case cash is needed urgently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I urge the Government to continue building research into the policy of implementation through randomised controlled trials so as to discover the most effective means of getting high take-up of MRSS.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Whilst CPF LIFE plays a key role in providing the basic level of retirement income for every Singaporean, it is inadequate as the sole source of post-retirement income to support a "reasonable" standard of living in retirement, unless the retirees are willing to make substantial compromises in their desired lifestyles, through to the end of life.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: A key policy recommendation of the report is to increase private savings with reforms to minimise investment management costs and enable individuals to benefit from collective investment management, at low cost, yet protecting the retirement savings from unprecedented low and negative interest rates and volatility of market cycles.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, in Singapore, it has been more than three years since the CPF Advisory Panel highlighted the significant investment costs and risks faced by retail investors in the current CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS).

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Panel had recommended that the Government introduce a new scheme, CPF Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme (CPF LRIS) as a prudent, professionally managed, low fee option for CPF members to invest and grow their "surplus" CPF retirement savings.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The improvement in net investment returns from the reduced investment costs, as well as the benefits from a professionally managed lifecycle fund, will significantly improve retirement adequacy, especially if compounded over a long-term period.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, I calculated that, over a 30-year period, a savings of 2% in investment management cost will translate to almost doubling the original sum, even before accounting to the growth of the underlining amount.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What are the difficulties and concerns in launching such a scheme?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Chairman, Sir, last year in August, the Government announced that the CPF contribution rates for older workers would be increased gradually starting from 2021 and carried out over the next 10 years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have called for the restoration of the full rate for all older workers, but I can also understand the Government's position that there is a need to balance the demand-side of the labour market, that is, the employability of older workers who are usually more expensive for employers, and the supply-side, that is, the incentives and sense of worth for older workers to remain in the labour market.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I understand this balance is worked out in intense tripartite discussions among employers, unions and the Government.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How said the Government is.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Minster Josephine Teo also said last year that the Government was committed despite the economic uncertainties faced by businesses in the context of the US-China trade war.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Now that the COVID-19 emergency is certain to hit the global economy and our open economy hard, I hope the Government is still committed to an increase.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I would like today to elaborate on why cost has been an issue for some, and why such a proposal need not affect retirement adequacy.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: We are all aware of the Adapt and Grow initiatives and how they dovetail into the Government's Industry Transformation Maps.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: These give effect to the broad national plan to enable the workforce to have relevant skills to take on jobs that are projected to be in demand now and in the future economy.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I appreciate the deliberations, consultations, planning and resources that have been devoted to this national endeavour, which has helped many mid-career employees find meaningful work in new industries.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Indeed, many courses endorsed under these frameworks are relatively low-cost and accessible.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: However, there are also other mid-career transitioners who will not be content with these offerings.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Some have remarked to me that to set themselves apart in a soft job market, they did not want a certification that so many others were already getting but to chart their own paths.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Some may already have tertiary qualifications and wish to do postgraduate courses in new areas conducted by overseas universities or professional bodies.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Others may want to venture to work abroad, where the skill areas in demand may not be the same as those under Singapore's economic transformation plan.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For these mid-career transitioners, the passion to take ownership of their own futures should be commended.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I agree that retirement adequacy will always be the overarching aim of the CPF savings scheme.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: However, reskilling potentially leads to better salary outcomes and could pay for itself.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This is important at a time where retirement and re-employment ages are moving up.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Government could always put in safeguards, such as has been done with the CPF investment schemes.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Patrick Tay, take both your cuts, please.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: In order to avoid conflicts of interest and undermining management effectiveness, executives with senior management functions were excluded from collective representation.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: These functions are set out in section 17(3) of the Industrial Relations Act.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: The tripartite partners have also issued the Tripartite Guidelines on Extending the Scope of Union Representation for Executives.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: The unions' experience, therefore, is that the exclusions set out in section 17(3) are too broadly worded, thereby giving employers the opportunity to claim that even mid-level executive employees fall within them, whereas the intent behind the law was only to exclude those who are at senior management levels and carrying out functions which genuinely give rise to a conflict of interest if they are represented by a union.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Besides this, there are other areas, such as the status of Collective Agreements during a Judicial Management or Receivership and whether the scope of coverage of the Collective Agreement can be limited to union members only, and several other procedural and technical areas which are unclear.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: This will help to better reflect the true intent of the law, look after the interests and welfare of workers and help employers and unions to reach consensus on extension of scope and other areas of industrial relations smoothly and expeditiously.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: In light of the expected growth of freelance workers or what many term as the "gig economy" in the next five to 10 years, the Labour Movement hopes more can be done to enable this group to become union members so that they, too, can enjoy the plethora of membership privileges NTUC and our unions offer.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Freelancers who are in a "contract for service" may not be full-fledged union members per se.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, let me start by updating Members on the labour market in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore Citizens continued to earn higher incomes in the recent five years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, if we look back over a longer period since 2015, the employment outcomes for our people have been very positive overall.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the COVID-19 outbreak, it would be unrealistic to expect employment growth of the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will also be a challenge for unemployment to remain in the relatively low range of recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These unfavourable conditions demand a united response from all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond immediate relief, we must not neglect future challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the longer term, we need businesses to transform and keep creating good jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We want wages at the lower end to move up more.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also need to help Singaporeans adapt to changing job requirements brought about by technology.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The resident workforce will not expand as much as before and we have more seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will need to help both businesses and our people make the best of the opportunities available.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, we must address their anxieties and be sure to walk this journey together.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM’s responses centre on the belief that there must be fairness at work, for both individuals and employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is essential to maintaining cohesiveness in an open economy, to give our workers fair chances to progress, and our businesses fair support to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will be speaking on four areas: fair opportunities, fair hiring, fair competition and fair support.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many Members of Parliament also asked that we offer more help to SEPs who have been hard hit.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I share their concerns and will announce more measures to support our freelancers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad will elaborate on how we can give fair support for lower-wage workers and employers of persons with disabilities (PwDs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He will cover foreign workers as well as their employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will elaborate on how we are providing fair opportunities for women, as well as fair support for foreign domestic workers (FDWs) and their employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our aim is to give every Singaporean every opportunity to progress at every stage of their working lives.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More than half were aged 40 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nearly one-third of placements were aged 50 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The share was even higher for rank-and-file workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, since 2016, the Adapt and Grow initiative, which includes the CSP, has helped over 100,000 jobseekers get placed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But we are mindful that the work is never done.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, Workforce Singapore (WSG) continues to enhance its service and programme offerings.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, MyCareersFuture.sg has new features to help employers identify suitable candidates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One particular group we have been thinking about are Singaporeans in their 40s and 50s.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They, too, deserve fair opportunities to progress in their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We recognise that it is a daunting task for anyone in the middle of their careers to reskill for new jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This was highlighted by Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Ms Jessica Tan and other Members of Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In response, the Government has put together the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mid-career individuals generally hope that their time invested in training leads to a job.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is why many programmes are "Place-and-Train" where a jobseeker first secures placement with the employer or attachment with a host company on the strength of his existing work experience and undergoes additional training to close the skills gap to fully meet job requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most participants on such programmes start their training only after they have been placed with an employer or a host company.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Forty-nine-year-old Shah Jehan Haniffa and 61-year-old Low Kok Chuen are two examples.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Despite limited experience in the logistics industry, Shah Jehan secured a job with ST Logistics through the PCP for Logistics Executives.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Low Kok Chuen decided to start work again after two years in retirement and enter a new industry.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Delphic Manufacturing Solution saw his potential and hired him through the PCP for Technical Sales Engineers or Managers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since 2016, "Place-and-Train" programmes have benefited nearly 14,500 Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, we have no shortage of such programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For PCPs alone, we have around 100 across around 30 sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To Mr Patrick Tay's question, in the last two years, over 2,000 professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) were reskilled and redeployed within the same companies, well before they became redundant.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To Ms Sylvia Lim's question, capacity is rarely the issue.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nonetheless, to support more mid-career individuals who may be affected by the faster pace of business transformation, we will expand capacity in such programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A good example is the TeSA Mid-Career Advance programme announced earlier by Minister Iswaran.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is the first pillar of the Mid-Career Support Package.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even then, Members of Parliament, like Mr Ong Teng Koon, are rightly concerned about employer commitment becoming the bottleneck.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Indeed, when programme capacity is not fully taken up, it is often because employers are hesitant.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Especially when prospects are uncertain, employers might hold back and wait for better conditions or a candidate with better match.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the other hand, employers continue to tell MOM their frustrations that mid-career jobseekers shun certain occupations or industries.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Jobseekers may lack awareness of the opportunities or confidence in their abilities to adapt to new work environments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some employers also need to improve job quality to make them more attractive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, beyond expanding the capacity of reskilling programmes, the Mid-Career Support Package must empower individuals and enable employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This aims to empower persons in their 40s and 50s to refresh their skills to complement their employers' training investments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Bear in mind that many courses are already heavily subsidised by the Government, up to 90% in some instances.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This additional top-up will mean even lower out-of-pocket expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These programmes do not require employer commitment upfront.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But, as long as the programmes are well-designed to plug skills-in-demand, participants have a good chance of getting job placements after they are trained.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) Committee of Supply (COS) debate, Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will share more details.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I hope it will persuade Ms Sylvia Lim that actually you do not touch CPF.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even the IHLs will be able to offer very good opportunities to help mid-careerists progress.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For "Place-and-Train" programmes, all trainees receive full salaries or allowances.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, during the nine months of PCP, Shah Jehan, whom I cited earlier, received full salary from his employer, 90% of which was subsidised by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, although we do not have unemployment insurance in Singapore, we have programmes that provide income support to unemployed persons who are prepared to undergo reskilling, which maximises their chances of returning to work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To empower mid-career individuals, another important pillar is our career advisory system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is the scaffolding and handholding that I spoke about in response to Ms Sylvia Lim's points during the Budget Debate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: WSG and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) have been offering employment and training assistance for well over a decade.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since the SkillsFuture movement was launched, the five Community Development Councils (CDCs) have also been mobilised.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About three years ago, we roped in the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Two best-in-class operators with good track records in other countries were appointed to supplement Government efforts in career-matching.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, for example, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Institute of Banking and Finance released a joint study on the impact of automation and data analytics on 121 job roles in financial services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I know that Mr Patrick Tay read this publication from cover to cover.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Amongst several outcomes, the Technology in Finance Immersion Programme was launched.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Leon Perera will be reassured to know that other agencies are conducting similar studies to help with workforce and career planning.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: WSG has also intensified support to jobseekers through a suite of high-touch career coaching programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Career Recharger module equips discouraged jobseekers with a positive mindset for their job search journeys.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Career Catalyst module offers one-on-one coaching to help jobseekers uncover their strengths and career options.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Career 360 module helps jobseekers access networks to widen their job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In this regard, peer support can be very useful.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is untapped potential in our professional communities where many seasoned professionals have rich experiences to share.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Career advisors will receive training to provide sector and occupation-specific career advice and outline career options.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Career advisors will also be equipped with in-depth knowledge of resources and channels of support, such as the Adapt and Grow programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In short, we hope that the career advisors can help to boost the confidence of their mid-career peers in charting the way forward.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, as the IHLs ramp up Train-and-Place programmes, they will also need to be better at providing career advice to mid-career individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM and MOE will work together to consolidate our resources and boost our collective capabilities in empowering individuals to take charge of their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In terms of support to employers, the priority is to bring down the cost of recruiting and training for mid-career jobseekers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must also keep up the pace of business transformation and job redesign.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This pillar comes on top of very generous funding already available for the training components.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Essentially, the Government will underwrite almost the entire salary and training costs of mid-career recruits for the period of training.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Further, we will provide a new incentive for employers who hire workers aged 40 and above, through any Place-and-Train or Train-and-Place programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How will be pleased to know that the enhanced employers support extends to workers above age 60.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Depending on the duration of training, this means employers will get salary support of up to one year in most cases.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is not even including the Senior Employment Credit, which I will talk more about later.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond these two pillars, the Government is providing another two pillars of support for employers to implement business and workforce transformation plans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is the reason for the $10,000 SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit which the Ministry of Trade and Industry has highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through the enhanced Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG), we will also provide up to 70% funding for companies to engage job redesign consultants.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is important for ensuring that jobs become more attractive, especially to mid-career individuals and seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most of the remaining 30% out-of-pocket expenses can be paid off using the new SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, costs will be very minimal, for SMEs in particular.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Douglas Foo and Mr Gan Thiam Poh were understandably concerned that employers may no longer be short of training funds but training time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For companies with a clear plan to transform their business, MOM will consider supporting them with transitionary manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Others may take advantage of the current downtime to increase training hours.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are a clear commitment to ensure Singaporeans have fair opportunities to progress at every stage of their working lives.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, we will need employers to uphold the culture of fairness at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This means taking care to ensure there is no discrimination of any kind.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In Singapore, where the workforce includes foreigners, we are particularly watchful about discrimination against locals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under FCF, we require employers to advertise on MyCareersFuture.sg before submitting EP applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is to ensure fair hiring and guard against job openings being restricted to "closed circles of friends".

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Murali Pillai pointed out that job positions with a salary of $15,000 and above are currently exempted from the FCF job advertising requirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This threshold was last updated in July 2018, when we also required smaller firms with at least 10 employees to advertise.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Positions that are more senior remain exempted as they are more likely to be market-sensitive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As for intra-company transfers, which Mr Patrick Tay asked about, they need to meet strict criteria to qualify.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a result, they have constituted a very small share of EP applicants.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will take this opportunity to remind employers not to treat the advertising requirement as a paper exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM has started to use data analytics to scrutinise EP applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I cannot tell you too much about it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, I cannot tell you what the algorithm is.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also actively follow up on leads provided by whistleblowers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members will appreciate that this is a laborious exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sometimes, disgruntled employees or competitors send us on a wild goose chase.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers may also use delay tactics to frustrate us.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nonetheless, if we uncover evidence that an employer had preselected a foreign candidate and did not give fair consideration to qualified local applicants, we will reject the EP application and ban the employer from hiring or renewing foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under FCF, MOM has also proactively identified employers suspected of nationality-bias in their hiring.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We look out for employers with an exceptionally high share of foreign PMETs compared to their industry peers or high concentrations of single nationalities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These employers are put on an FCF Watchlist, where all of the EP applications will be scrutinised or withheld.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Among other Members of Parliament, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked for an update on these efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I informed Parliament last year that MOM had put about 600 firms through the FCF Watchlist.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have since cast our net wider and scrutinised about 1,000 firms.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, firms under FCF have hired more than 4,400 Singaporean PMETs over the same period.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our objective is not just to penalise errant employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we reached out to another 350 employers whose workforce profiles give us cause for concern, so that they take additional steps to strengthen local hiring.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But it also means that having served notice to these employers, MOM will not hesitate to put them on the FCF Watchlist if their workforce profiles deteriorate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nationality bias is only one form of discrimination.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I agree with Mr Lim Biow Chuan that we should take firm action against all forms of discrimination.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why I announced earlier this year stiffer penalties for discrimination by age, gender, nationality or mental health condition.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In one case, a 51-year-old applying to be a receptionist was told that she was "too old".

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM discovered that the firm had a policy where only candidates younger than 45, female and Chinese, would be invited for interview.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also hold culpable key decision-makers responsible, whether it is the chief executive officer (CEO), the chief HR officer (CHRO) or line managers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are prepared to name them publicly and revoke their work passes if they are foreigners.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some people may feel that the penalties are still not enough.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most of the work passes will expire during this period but none can be renewed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Neither can the employer hire new foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, these employers would need to hire more locals if they want to continue their operations in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM will also prosecute employers and key personnel who make false declarations on fair consideration.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to remain vigilant against discriminatory employers and take firm action against those who try to circumvent our fair hiring requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Workers who come across workplace discrimination should surface it to MOM or TAFEP.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers should review employment practices to weed out discriminatory practices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employer organisations should call out members with errant practices that tarnish their sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides the assurance of fair hiring, our people want the assurance that they compete on a level playing field.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Fair-minded Singaporeans do not expect to be given a free pass but they do expect fair competition, and rightly so.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat, we will implement cuts to S Pass quotas for the construction, marine shipyard and process sectors in 2021 and 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As he explained, S Passes should not be a means by which enterprises hire low-cost foreigners when qualified locals are available.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked what jobs were available in these sectors and what we were doing to train locals for them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In construction, for example, there is growing demand for PMETs skilled in Building Information Modelling (BIM) to use advanced software to visualise and manage building projects.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many draughtsmen who previously made technical drawings are now taking on more complex BIM roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Other jobs performed by technicians and engineers will be equally transformed by automation and digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our educational institutions already work closely with industries to ensure their students have the right training.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From 2017 to 2019, there was an annual average intake of 7,400 polytechnic students in related courses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For mid-career persons, we have PCPs for BIM Professionals, Marine Engineers, Marine Technicians, and Process Construction and Maintenance Professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am aware that affected businesses may still be worried they cannot find people.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is unlikely that locals will change their minds if work conditions do not improve.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But as long as employers are willing to make changes, we will help them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The SkillsFuture Work-Study Programme can help you identify suitable polytechnic and Institute of Technical Education (ITE) graduates and help to defray training costs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have outlined the enhanced support for employers under the Mid-Career Support Package.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I urge employers to get in touch with WSG or the relevant trade associations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, in the last three years, TACs have helped more than 4,500 SMEs recruit mid-career PMETs through the P-Max programme – one programme alone.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides quotas, we regularly review other measures to control the foreign workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To ensure that firms do not hire locals on token salaries just so that they can hire more foreign workers, only workers that are paid above a threshold each month can be counted towards a firm's S Pass and Work Permit DRCs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We call this the Local Qualifying Salary (LQS).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have been regularly updating the LQS to ensure that it keeps pace with rising local wages at the lower end.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most employers of foreign workers are not affected because they do not have workers earning below $1,400.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even for those that are, the extension of the Wage Credit Scheme should provide some relief.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In any case, like Ms Denise Phua and Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, I hope employers and their customers do not begrudge the raising of salaries at the lower end.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the S Pass and EP levels, MOM regularly updates the salary criteria that applicants must meet to work in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These criteria take reference from salaries of locals with similar experience and seniority to ensure that the S Pass and EP holders are of good calibre and do not undercut the wages of our local PMETs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why older and more experienced candidates need to command higher salaries in order to qualify for a S Pass or an EP.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This increase is in line with improving wages of fresh graduates of local autonomous universities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The salary criteria for older and more experienced EP candidates will be raised in tandem.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, an EP applicant in his early 40s will need to earn around double the new minimum qualifying salary of $3,900; double of $3,900.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is only fair, considering the skillsets he or she is expected to have.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It helps to ensure a level playing field for experienced local mid-career PMETs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This staggered approach will moderate the impact on businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With these changes, employers should continue to ensure that they have fair and merit-based pay practices, in line with the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Anecdotally, we have heard of firms that only raise salaries of the EP holders to meet new salary criteria, while freezing salaries of the local workers, even if the locals are better performers!

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is wrong and not in the employer's best interest.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Apart from the risk of having their work pass privileges cut back by MOM, such practices will undermine their efforts to retain their local employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we are asking a lot more of our employers, we are also providing them with fair support.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Likewise, we will give fair support to the self-employed and for Singaporeans in general to build up their retirement nest-egg.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the past decade, senior employment rates among locals have grown steadily.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2018, I convened the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers to study ways to further support senior employment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It announced its recommendations last year, which the Government has accepted in full.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Retirement Age (RA) and the Re-employment Age (REA) will be raised to 65 and 70 respectively by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To help businesses adjust, each move will be implemented in small steps with sufficient notice.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, the CPF contribution rates for senior workers will be raised gradually over the next decade.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The first increase will take effect from 1 January 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The exact timing of future moves will be decided later, but we aim to implement the full increases by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Yesterday, Minister Shanmugam announced that the retirement age for Home Affairs Uniformed Services will be raised from age 55 to 58 by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM welcomes this move and will work with the Ministry of Home Affairs and our tripartite partners to similarly review retirement age policies for Auxiliary Police Officers and private-sector firefighters.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Businesses had called for continued Government support for the employment of senior workers, in particular, wage offsets similar to the Special Employment Credit (SEC).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From 2021, through the new SEC, we will provide wage offsets to employers that hire senior Singaporean workers aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For 2021 and 2022, employers will get up to 8% of the wages paid to workers aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Similar to SEC, more support will be given for those in higher age bands.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The employment rate for workers aged 55-59 has improved greatly and is now close to that of the 20-64 age group.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Hence, wage offsets for the 55-59 age group will be 2% in 2021 and 1% in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will instead focus resources on the older age groups which have lower employment rates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Wage offsets for those aged 67 and above will be the highest, at 8%.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Overall, companies will get $660 million in SEC over two years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2021, we will offset half of the increase in employer CPF contribution rates through the CPF Transition Offset scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are not depending on the SEC alone to support senior employment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We encourage progressive companies to raise the RA and REA ahead of legislative schedule.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And to do so, we will introduce a Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant (EAG).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Companies can get up to $250,000 each under this grant.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through the Tripartite Workgroup's public consultation and other surveys, senior workers told us they would like to reduce their work intensity gradually as they approach retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are also more prepared to remain in the workforce if they can undertake part-time work arrangements during the re-employment phase.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While the Tripartite Workgroup explored legislating the provision of part time re-employment, employers expressed serious concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Their work structures and processes cannot support workers on partial shifts, or job sharing of full-time positions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This explains our relatively low part-time employment rate for seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Workgroup agreed on a promotional approach to give employers time to adjust.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will benefit seniors who prefer lower work intensity, thereby encouraging them to stay in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, let me now address the concerns of SEPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Based on our most recent survey, the share of individuals who took on self-employed work as their main job remained stable at around 8% to 10% of our resident workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most of our SEPs have a preference for self-employment over regular employment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A small number would actually prefer to be in regular employment but could not find suitable openings.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We encourage them to approach WSG or e2i which will help them through the relevant programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While some SEPs ponder their longer-term plans, the immediate concern of all is the significant drop in earnings due to the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sector agencies are stepping in to help those directly impacted.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, the Ministry of Transport has put together a $77 million package to help taxi and private hire care drivers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Singapore Tourism Board (STB) is also providing licensed tour guides with short-term relief.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEPs in other occupations may see lower earnings because their clients have delayed projects or postponed bookings.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is, no doubt, a period of difficulty.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But it is also a window of opportunity for skills upgrading.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will, therefore, introduce a new SEP Training Support Scheme, which I believe Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Ang Hin Kee, Mr Desmond Choo, Ms Tin Pei Ling and other Members of Parliament will welcome.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not only will this scheme supplement their income, it can help them become more future-ready.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To illustrate, consider a 45-year-old freelance sports coach or media freelancer who decides to brush up on business management skills by taking a series of courses covering areas, such as digital marketing and design thinking.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Together, there are six modular courses stretching over 90 hours or about 12 days.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With SkillsFuture Singapore's (SSG's) enhanced 90% subsidy of the course fees for those aged 40 and above, this sports coach or media freelancer would only need to pay about $400 for the course.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And by using his SkillsFuture Credit, he will not need to pay a single cent out of his pocket.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Furthermore, he will receive training allowance of $675.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The SEP Training Support Scheme is a practical way to provide fair support to SEPs in these tough times.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is no cap to how much training SEPs can sign up for.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: NTUC, which has established outreach channels to freelancers, will administer this scheme and release details on how to apply soon.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as we support SEPs in the short term, we are also concerned about their longer-term needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2017, the Government set up the Tripartite Workgroup on SEPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through extensive consultations with stakeholders, the Workgroup found that most SEPs did not expect their clients to provide employment benefits or to treat them as regular employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, SEPs asked the Workgroup to focus on addressing their practical concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Their preference shaped the Workgroup's recommendations, which have been progressively implemented since March 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management extended its services to SEPs to help resolve payment-related disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also launched the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs to promote fair contracting norms and have made good progress.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Grab, a major player in the private hire car and food delivery markets, recently adopted this Standard, joining about 710 other progressive businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This means that the 85,000 SEPs engaged by these adopters will be provided with clear written terms to minimise disputes, such as when payments would be made.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We call on more service-buyers to do their part by providing SEPs with clear written contracts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also encourage service buyers to adopt the Standard, to be more attractive among SEPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are committed to providing fair support to help our people prepare for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, successive cohorts of Singaporeans have been able to set aside more CPF savings for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the last decade, median CPF balances of active CPF members aged 55 have also more than doubled from $71,000 to $155,000.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is because of higher labour force participation and rising wages as well as enhancements to the CPF system, such as the increases in CPF contribution rates and CPF salary ceiling.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That does not mean our job is done.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The CPF is a "live" system and must continue to evolve.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
