text: Incomes continue to rise and so will spending needs in retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why the Government accepted the Tripartite Workgroup's recommendation to gradually raise CPF contribution rates for senior workers over the next 10 years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked if we could accelerate the pace.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But this desire needs to be balanced against the impact on the senior workers' employability and take-home pay, factors which he himself had outlined.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why CPF contribution rates should continue to be stepped down by age and why the Workgroup recommended small increases each time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the current pressures on employers and job security, we should proceed with care.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the years, we have also refined our retirement system to be fairer and more progressive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government provides higher interest rates of up to 6% on lower CPF balances.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government also tops up the CPF accounts of lower balance members from time to time, such as the recent Bicentennial Bonus CPF top-up.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Targeted subsidies are provided to lower-income Singaporeans with lesser means, through Workfare in their working years and Silver Support in retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All these translate into substantial support for lower-income households in retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government will take additional steps to strengthen retirement adequacy of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We launched the CAYE pilot at the start of the year to help SEPs better save for their healthcare needs through smaller and more regular MediSave contributions whenever they earn income.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We expect about 3,000 SEPs or so working with Government agencies each year to make CAYE contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To help SEPs come on board the scheme, we will provide a dollar-for-dollar matching for CAYE contributions made in 2020, capped at $600.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao will be pleased to note that around 400 SEPs made CAYE contributions in January alone.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All of them will receive matched MediSave contributions from the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEPs can also save for retirement through cash top-up schemes into their CPF.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those who are eligible can tap on the MRSS, which I will elaborate on later.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, SEPs may receive additional support through the WIS Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From 1 January 2020, the qualifying income cap and maximum annual payouts have both gone up.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, recipients will get an additional 20% of their WIS payment for work done in 2019, with a minimum payment of $100.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Each year, more than 50,000 SEPs receive WIS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With the COVID-19 situation, I expect more SEPs to qualify this year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More broadly, to help Singaporeans with less CPF savings, we will introduce MRSS from 2021 to 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This can benefit lower-income seniors and, in particular, gig workers and "unpaid" caregivers, who typically have less in their CPF.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government will match cash top-ups made to the RA of eligible members, up to $600 annually or $3,000 over five years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About 435,000 Singaporeans will be eligible for MRSS each year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are no restrictions on who can contribute.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, employers may want to use MRSS as a staff benefit to recognise long-serving senior workers and help them set aside more for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They will enjoy tax reliefs for cash top-ups.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Working adults can also make top-ups to their stay-at-home spouses, or their parents who are nearing retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira is not so sure and suggested that people be asked to commit their savings in advance, for example, their WIS cash payouts or annual bonuses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will study seriously the practicalities of his suggestion.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Silver Support targets seniors who had lower incomes throughout their lives and have less in their retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since 2016, we have disbursed close to $1.6 billion to over 200,000 seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With these enhancements, close to 250,000 Singaporeans aged 65 and above will benefit in 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM will continue to review our policies to improve the retirement adequacy of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes studying the feasibility of introducing the CPF LRIS, which Ms Foo Mee Har asked about.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: LRIS will be designed for members who wish to invest their CPF monies but have neither the knowledge nor time to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To be attractive, it has to charge low fees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There must be a good chance of earning higher returns than the current CPF interest rates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But it should also provide some assurance against the downside risks.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a complex effort with many multiple objectives that are not always consistent with one another.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the many issues that demand MOM's time, I seek Members' understanding that we need more time to get the fundamentals of LRIS right.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to conclude in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, at the moment, the economic outlook of the whole world is unclear.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is not only due to COVID-19 but also because of technological advancement that is constantly changing the nature of jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the face of these key external factors, Singaporeans may be concerned about their employment prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government will do everything it can to protect the rice bowls of our people.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, those in their 40s and 50s are at a stage of life where they need to support their families.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides caring for their aged parents and school-going children, most of them are still paying off their home mortgage.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are worried that even if they work hard, they cannot avoid becoming obsolete.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, the Government has strengthened its efforts to focus on middle-age workers in their 40s and 50s, so that they can take charge of their careers, explore new opportunities and carve out new careers for themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We understand that if we want to help these workers, we need the cooperation of employers and enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our reskilling efforts would not achieve the intended outcome if they are not supported by employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As they say, the number 66 is symbolic of a smooth-sailing pathway.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We hope that employers can keep an open mind and give more opportunities for mid-career and middle-age workers to play a greater role.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, many companies in Singapore are supportive of the Government's policies, especially with regard to hiring senior workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As the Chinese saying goes: 家有一老，如有一宝， an elder in the family is a treasure.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I hope employers will adopt the same attitude towards senior workers within their companies, and help them achieve their aspirations to work longer and accumulate more savings.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, the more "elders" they retain or re-employ, the more "treasures" they will receive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the last few weeks, the Government has announced various packages to help taxi drivers, Grab drivers and tour guides.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: NTUC will administer the SEP Training Support Scheme to help SEPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If they undergo training under the SkillsFuture Series or sector specific-training programmes, they will receive up to $60 per day for attending the courses, on top of the existing subsidies on course fees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is no cap on how much training they can sign up for.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, I would urge SEPs to make good use of these schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not only will they enjoy wage subsidies, they can also learn a new skill.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a society, we should pay more attention to assist the more vulnerable groups who have less in retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From this year, we will enhance the Workfare programme to benefit more low-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Silver Support Scheme has benefited 150,000 workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From the end of this year, the quarterly cash supplement will increase by 20%.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Next year, we will further expand the criteria to include an additional 100,000 senior workers to benefit from this scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to refine these schemes to benefit those with less in retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond these initiatives, the Government will help Singaporeans build up more retirement savings to prepare them for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government is committed to ensuring job security for everyone and look after disadvantaged groups.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even in this time when the economic impact of the COVID-19 outbreak is still unclear, we are fortunate that we still have the means to develop long-term plans to lay a good foundation for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I firmly believe that in spite of the immediate challenges and difficulties, we can create a better home for all as long as we work together as one Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, in recent years, NTUC and the Government, with the support of our tripartite stakeholders, have taken bold and specific interventions to help workers, providing essential services with better wages, better welfare and better work prospects because every worker matters.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Other schemes implemented over the years, such as the Workfare Scheme, have helped them with cost of living and hope for a better future through new skills that they can acquire at heavily subsidised rates.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The road to improving the lives of low-wage workers cannot just end here.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that the SkillsFuture framework, identifying different job levels and skills for more than 30 sectors, have been developed, it would be easier to develop the wage ladder for some industries.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This would incentivise workers, especially low-wage workers, to upgrade themselves if the prospect for better wages are assured.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: NTUC will put up some possible sectors and hope the Government will give due consideration.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Previously, I have also on several occasions in Parliament made calls for Annual Wage Supplement (AWS) to be made mandatory, especially for low-wage workers, but the response so far has been, at best, lukewarm.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many of us assume that all workers get the 13th month bonus or AWS at the end of the year.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But the sad reality is that the very group that needs it most is not receiving it.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As a society, we must demand for the right treatment of our low-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As the Government has pledged to support outcome-based procurement practices, perhaps the Government and Government-linked companies can also nudge employers towards the right behaviour, to award tenders to companies with good HR practices that include paying the 13th month bonus as part of their pay package.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have also called for better protection of low-wage workers against unfair employment contracts and terms.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have highlighted this in a blogpost that I wrote last year.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Chairman, most of our lower-wage workers are in sectors where their wages have stagnated due to competitive outsourcing practices.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: PWM puts in place a systematic framework to track the quality of work, gains in productivity and training attained by these workers and peg them to corresponding wage increments and career progression.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: PWM has proven to be effective in uplifting workers in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors and improved their prospects.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: In addition, I would like to request for measures to ensure that these workers have access to proper rest areas and safe work environments backed by legislation and regular enforcement.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As Minister Josephine Teo has just mentioned, there is also a suite of other support measures on job support, wage credit, enterprise grants and so on.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is clear that reskilling and staying relevant are applicable to everyone and are an effort played by all – individual, employers, society and the Government.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But what does this mean to the people with special needs or disabilities?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Some that I spoke to raised the challenges they face at the workplace.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In a nutshell, finding and sustaining employment in life for them is a constant challenge.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In this regard, I would like to ask MOM what can be done to better facilitate job design and assignment of jobs for people with special needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Which policy area can be improved to raise awareness and protect their rights at work?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: How much to disclose and when to do so are always key concerns for these individuals who feel they are disadvantaged from the start.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Employers and colleagues can create the right work culture, one that focuses on establishing shared interests and values, building bridges with them and connect through common grounds.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: They need to be treated as people, not labour.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: By not emphasising their conditions also means inclusion, as all are accepted as one.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: There needs to be a better match in mutual expectations, understanding the intrinsic ability of the staff and assigning appropriate task, recognising their contribution and lending emotional support are important.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Unfair judgement or biased treatment will only result in clashes or poor work performance.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Sometimes, special needs people also require occasional medical treatments throughout their life.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Being flexible in work arrangements or time off will help them when annual leave is limited and for those whose physique or stamina are constrained by the number of hours they can put in each day.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Third, enhance the dedicated resources of job referral and training organisations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Job coaching, preparatory for workplace and reskilling are fundamental for people with special needs to continue being in the workforce and remain in the industries.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Some form of assistance do exist today but the period of support is short.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: If the Government and the agencies can play a more prominent role in matching their skills and appropriate employers, this acts as a safeguard for them to remain connected in the industries.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Employers and job coaches who value such employees should also be ready to provide testimonials and be willing to offer as their referrals for future jobs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Lastly, equality in terms and conditions of work.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is not uncommon to hear that people with special needs are often grateful that they are being offered a job and would remain in the job for a long time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But they are, in fact, no different from other workers when they put their heart to the tasks.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I hope to see stronger support and movement towards levelling the playing field for people with special needs in the area of employment and lifelong learning.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The National Council of Social Services (NCSS) published its "Quality of Life Study on Persons with Disabilities" in 2016.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The study involved close to 1,000 respondents with disabilities.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The study incorporated a face-to-face survey which sought to identify the needs of persons with disabilities (PwDs) across six domains of Quality of Life.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: NCSS carried out another study with 1,400 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs) on attitudes towards PwDs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deeper probing suggests that the public often perceives a person's disability as the inability to perform one's job.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In particular, it was found that people in general feel or behave even less positively towards individuals with autism or intellectual disabilities.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Information on both studies can be found in this publication by NCSS.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As I have said before in this House, being gainfully employed and being able to be remunerated for doing meaningful work, like other typical hires, are a start in helping PwDs with special needs live independently like many others and it accords suﬃcient opportunities for them to develop that much-needed sense of identity, self-esteem and self-dignity.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Government has introduced schemes, such as the Special Employment Credit (SEC), Workfare Training Scheme (WTS) and the Open Door Programme (ODP) to help PwDs with special needs to be employed.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, how many employers actually have, in their hiring policies and practices, aﬃrmative action to employ PwDs with special needs?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many employers have leveraged these schemes to actively hire persons with disabilities or special needs?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will there be a new Employment Credit scheme to help employers employ PwDs with special needs?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Or can the SEC be extended to employers to continue employing PwDs with special needs?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I laud the Adapt and Grow and Place-and-Train initiatives available for older workers and for students to upgrade and transition into the world of work across sectors, such as hotel, retail, food services, tourism and air transport.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will there be a similar Place-and-Train scheme for PwDs with special needs to help them ease into their new job and place of work and learn on-the-job?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am sure sectors, such as food services, retail and tourism, are always in need of employees and these are sectors where PwDs with special needs can do well in, provided they are given the opportunity and are coached to perform their job functions well.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In last year's COS, I brought up the need to provide decent working conditions, such as the provision of proper rest areas for lower-wage and outsourced workers, such as cleaners, security oﬃcers, food and beverage service staﬀ and despatch riders.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I had also expressed that while some people may feel that requiring proper rest areas is a trivial request, it is not so.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When you work the most part of the day on your feet, you do look forward to having a proper place to sit and rest and experience some sense of well-being while at work.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And this rest area should not be at staircases or rubbish dump areas.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I had requested MOM to make proper rest areas for lower-wage and outsourced workers mandatory.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These rest areas should be well-ventilated, well-lit and have proper tables and seats for the workers to have their meals and to rest.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Other than rest areas, there must be proper lockers where personal belongings can be stored safely while they work.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many employers and organisations have agreed to make such a provision for their lower-wage or outsourced workers?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How is MOM helping employers and organisations make this provision?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In the public consultation that my team and I conducted on mental health, there were 76 responses referencing issues within workplaces.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The focus of the Ministry on mental wellness within workplaces as part of the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) 2028 vision is prudent and necessary, as supported also by the World Health Organization (WHO).

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Will the Ministry consider issuing an advisory to employers to adopt progressive practices that support their employees’ mental health?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Countries, including the United Kingdom (UK) and Canada, have legislated the right to FWAs.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: One indicated that most treatment options for mental health conditions are only available on weekdays, with their employers unwilling to provide FWAs.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Given the Ministry’s strong endorsement for FWAs in caregiver support and Work-Life Grant, would the Ministry consider legislating the right of employees to pursue FWAs and also make explicit publicly that sick leave entitlement can be used for both physical and mental health conditions?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Six responses raised lack of mental health insurance as affecting treatment affordability.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: One respondent shared the inability to claim insurance for treatment at the Institute for Mental Health as the company insurer does not allow this.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The recent Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) amendment saw the Ministry working with a group of insurance companies to risk-pool and ensure affordable premiums for employers.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In a similar vein, will the Ministry consider working with insurance companies in providing mental health coverage for employees?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When I visited the funeral wake, the family was understandably distraught and they had many questions which the employer did not provide.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The company did not explain to the family how workmen insurance compensation worked, did not provide more information on whether the company had bought additional insurance and did not even provide the contact details of a person that the family could approach.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: No one explained to the family if they would get a factual report of what happened and, if so, from which entity.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, the fire left a Singaporean family with two young boys – six and four years old – without a father.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While much work for workplace safety has focused on prevention, I believe MOM must mandate that companies in high-risk industries put in place crisis management and family support best practices to ensure that families get the maximum amount of support when something goes wrong.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The situation could even be worse if an accident involves a sole breadwinner.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Meanwhile, I would also like to ask MOM to provide an update on our workplace safety and health record over the past year and if it is introducing additional measures to enhance WSH.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is a new low, but I believe we can strive to do better.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To achieve better workplace safety, it is important that we challenge ourselves constantly to make work conditions even safer and healthier for our workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the progress of the respective recommendations made then?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to reiterate my continued repeated calls for a mandatory WSH representative in every company.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will help to support the advocacy and implementation of WSH initiatives at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mental health, in particular, is vital for our overall well-being.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But while mental health issues are real and ever-present, particularly at our workplaces, many are afraid to voice out for fear of stigmatisation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Therefore, we need to raise awareness and socialise mental health issues so that we can build an ecosystem of support to help with the detection and early prevention of mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Labour Movement will do our part in destigmatising workplace mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We will recognise inclusive employers who have gone the extra mile to put in place robust mental wellness programmes to help employees stay mentally healthy and resilient.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Through profiling such inclusive employers as industry role models, we hope that we can encourage more companies to do the same.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope also that the Government will partner NTUC to study the incidence of workplace mental health issues and the effects, both long term and short term, that they have on our workforce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: By working together to create better total WSH outcomes at the workplace, I believe that our workers will have – to quote Mr Lim Swee Say – a Healthy and Happy, Productive and Purposeful (H2P2) life.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Zainal Sapari, you can take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: This begs the question whether the measures taken have been effective in reducing workplace fatalities involving migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: What is the result of the investigations and, if wrongdoing or negligence is found, when can we expect sanctions to be handed down?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Is MOM reviewing rules, increasing enforcement or doing anything else to ensure such spates are prevented in future?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: These gaps must be addressed systematically so that we can have truly inclusive and progressive practices in WSH because every worker matters and every job counts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Although the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act requires employers to switch to electronic payment should the workers request for it, the reality on the ground is that workers would be too afraid to push the issue should the employer refuse, for fear of termination and repatriation by employers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: This is an unacceptable consequence to most migrant workers, especially if they have paid high recruitment or placement fees to come here in the first place.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Are there statistics on what proportion of the WPH population is already paid electronically?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Given the success of the MWC-Post Office Savings Bank (POSB) Bank Account-Membership Programme, will MOM be able to say when mandatory electronic salary payment for WPHs can be a reality?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: MWC has been assisting migrant workers who sustain serious injuries from workplace accidents, including helping many employers discharge their responsibilities to their migrant workers undergoing treatment.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Even though employers can opt for a higher coverage, the reality is that many would opt for the lower coverage to manage their business costs.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: This would make the workers vulnerable if the final treatment cost is not covered by insurance and the employer is unable to bear the cost.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Every worker matters and it is important that they are taken care of in times of need.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.20 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.58 pm until 4.20 pm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, as the Minister for Manpower has shared, MOM will continue to champion fairness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Fairness in the workplace encompasses fair support for both employers and workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I will share our plans to enable inclusive growth for low-wage workers as well as persons with disabilities, and how we inculcate care for all workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the years, we have improved their wages and skills through various policies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A handout on the achievements of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) can be found on Members' seats.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked for an update on PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The current mandatory PWM framework has served us well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2018, we announced a PWM for the lift maintenance sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Ministry of National Development plans to make this mandatory in due course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Meanwhile, the Government is taking the lead by only awarding lift maintenance tenders to firms that have adopted PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari and Mr Lim Swee Say asked to expand the PWM to more sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We appointed a tripartite cluster to include escalator technicians under the lift PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together, close to 1,300 resident lift and escalator maintenance workers stand to benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Tripartite Cluster for Lift and Escalator Industry, the fourth such cluster, will aim to submit its recommendations by the end of the year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But we will not stop with these four clusters and intend to expand PWM to more sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So far, the sectors that implemented PWM have found that a mandatory approach, where a regulator imposes a uniform obligation to comply with PWM, delivers results most readily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If Government agencies are themselves large buyers of such services, Government procurement policies can also help to kickstart the process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, the vision of progressive wages, which Mr Lim Swee Say first laid out many years ago as Secretary-General of the NTUC, is more far-reaching than that.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is a vision that every sector should have a clear ladder for better jobs, better skills and, as a result, better wages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Therefore, even as we extend mandatory PWM to a few other sectors, we intend to introduce PWM even to sectors where we may not be able to apply mandatory PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want PWM to be a broader movement where the community can play a part as responsible consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under this approach, we want to create a virtuous cycle where companies that voluntarily pay progressive wages and provide job progression pathways to their low-wage workers are recognised and rewarded by consumers who support them by purchasing their products and services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will, in turn, spur more companies to be progressive as the best way to advance their business interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are working actively with our tripartite partners to explore how we can expand PWM in new sectors and with a new approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, we recognise there are current market challenges with COVID-19, and we will have to share more when the economic climate and business conditions are more favourable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Progressive wages are one way to support low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will replace WTS with a new Workfare Skills Support (WSS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the years, our workers have benefited from the introduction of substantial SkillsFuture course fee subsidies of up to 90% and SkillsFuture Credit for training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The old WTS came at a time before SkillsFuture established itself to what it is today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, therefore, there is a fair bit of duplication between WTS and SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under the new WSS, we will no longer provide course fee subsidies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Instead, WSS will provide more support for workers who complete training leading to full qualifications under the Singapore Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ), as well as the academic Continuing Education and Training (CET) qualification systems.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is because we have found that those who acquire full qualifications are more likely to earn higher wages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Forty-two-year-old Mr Syamsaini Ramli is one such example.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Syamsaini's employer, ParkRoyal Collection Marina Bay, used WTS to sponsor him for courses that led to a WSQ Certificate in Security Operations, a full qualification.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Syamsaini gained new skills in areas, such as counter-terrorism and managing threatening behaviour, which his employer valued.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He was promoted to assistant security supervisor in 2019, with a pay increment of 10%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Its annual cap will also be increased to $1,000, from $400.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also raise the training allowance to $6 per hour, from $4.50, to offset the opportunity costs of workers' training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will tie the eligibility for training allowance to courses which are more likely to lead to better employment outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our current programmes to support PwDs have contributed to their improving employment rate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, I shared that three in 10 of PwDs aged between 15 and 64 were in employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Between 2016 and 2019, more than 2,000 PwDs found new jobs through the Adapt and Grow (A&G) initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Open Door Programme (ODP), a special scheme under the A&G initiative, is administered by SG Enable, and helps PwDs enter suitable jobs and better integrate into the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It provides support for job placement, training and job redesign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM and SG Enable also launched the Job Redesign Guide to help companies better integrate PwDs into the workplace, one of the critical success factors for PwDs continuing to be employed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want to do more to improve the employment and employability of PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To study this, the Ministry of Social and Family Development set up the Enabling Masterplan workgroup comprising public, private and people sector representatives last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the workgroup's support, MOM will be enhancing our schemes to give our PwDs a boost.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The workgroup recognised that training and job redesign are key to helping PwDs stay employable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One of the beneficiaries of the ODP Training Grant is David.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: David was diagnosed with mild retina pigmentosa in his teens, which led to worsening vision over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He lost his job as an engineer in his mid-50s.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: David tapped on the ODP Training Grant to pick up workplace information technology (IT) skills as well as telephone etiquette.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The courses prepared him for an alternative career pathway as a call centre agent with Eureka Call Centre Systems (EurekaCCS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: EurekaCCS also tapped on the Job Redesign Grant to purchase keyboards with larger font keys and high colour contrast, allowing employees, such as David, to work more productively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The training David underwent gave him confidence to attend to enquiries and feedback from customers and David performed so well that EurekaCCS recognised him as one of their top performing call agents and rewarded him with an additional bonus incentive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In total, EurekaCCS has 14 employees with disabilities, who make up 87% of its workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope more employers will follow its lead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also raise the training allowance for both unemployed and employed PwDs to $6 per hour and introduce a training commitment award of $100 per completed eligible training course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SEC and ASEC have served our PWD employees well and will expire this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: EEC will be given to employers that hire Singaporean PwDs earning below $4,000 per month and this will cover about four in five of current PwD employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: EEC provides a wage offset of up to 20% of the employee's monthly income, capped at a maximum of $400 per month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In addition, employers hiring PwDs who have not been working for at least six months will receive an additional 10% wage offset, capped at $200 per month, for the first six months of employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Alvin Yeo, the founder of Faith Music Centre, is one employer who will benefit from the new EEC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Faith Music Centre is a social enterprise which teaches music to PwDs and has also hired several of the centre's learners with disabilities as music instructors and stage masters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, Faith Music Centre has 15 employees with varied disabilities, including autism spectrum disorder, sensory impairment and intellectual disability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: EEC will provide Faith Music Centre a larger wage offset as compared to SEC and even more support if they hire more PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As PwDs become more economically active, the issues of financial independence, whether they enjoy fair salaries, as raised by Dr Intan Azura as well as Miss Cheryl Chan, will become more important to PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM will closely monitor workplace practices and encourage progressive practices for PwDs, just as it does for other workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices, employers are expected to treat PwDs fairly, including asking for information only relevant to the job and paying them fairly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Lower-income PwDs also receive additional support through Workfare Income Supplement (WIS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2019, over 6,300 PwDs received WIS payouts amounting to $6.7 million.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: WIS has been further enhanced from 1 January 2020, with a higher qualifying income ceiling of $2,300 per month and higher maximum payouts of $4,000 per year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, ultimately, the best way to safeguard the interests of our PwDs is to ensure that they have many good opportunities to choose from.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This means more employers hiring PwDs and giving them opportunities for career growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It also means more Singaporeans welcoming PwDs as colleagues in the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond inclusive growth, we want to promote a culture of care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is important to uphold our workers' dignity and to support them by giving them the respect they deserve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, we launched Workcare, an initiative to uplift the well-being of our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To begin, we are focusing on rest areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Dr Intan Mokhtar asked for updates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In sites with space constraints, cleaners asked minimally for means to safekeep their belongings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) has worked with their cleaning contractors to provide lockers in 10 Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) hawker centres, and will do so for the remaining 16 centres by the end of 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Simple gestures, such as thanking these workers for their services, are small but significant ways that will improve their well-being and dignity at work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Yee Chia Hsing and Mr Zainal Sapari raised issues concerning WSH.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As we all know it, a culture of care includes ensuring the safety and health of our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And over the past decade, Singapore's WSH performance has improved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The workplace fatal injury rate last year was no worse than in 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More details will be released in the 2019 WSH Statistics Report by next week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In response to Mr Zainal Sapari, there was no dominant trend that contributed to the fatal accidents in November last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Where necessary, we will issue Stop Work Orders to prevent risks to other workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Stop Work Orders are minimally for three weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And companies have to rectify all unsafe conditions before Orders are lifted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If we find that companies or individuals have failed in their WSH obligations, we will prosecute them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I agree with Mr Zainal Sapari that the tripartite partners should do more to prevent accidents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This was what many of the WSH2028 recommendations sought to do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One of the underlying principles of WSH2028 is to make good WSH good for business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There will then be stronger impetus for firms to embed WSH in their culture and practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Later this year, designated WIC insurers will have access to potential clients' WIC claim records.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We expect insurers to set higher premiums for firms with poorer safety records.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, there is an impact to the premiums that you pay compared to how you perform at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We agree with Mr Melvin Yong that every company should have representatives to champion progressive WSH practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, making this mandatory in every company may not be practical.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, the WSH 2028 Tripartite Strategies Committee concluded that a prescriptive approach is not the way forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The more prudent approach is to promote this as a progressive practice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will support the Labour Movement in championing WSH representatives and other progressive WSH practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I agree fully with Mr Yee Chia Hsing that support for the families affected by workplace accidents is essential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I, too, visited the family in the constituency that was affected, and certainly, our hearts go out to the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It was a really tragic accident that I feel is needless.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM will sensitise employers, including through the Institute for HR professionals, because HR is usually the first interface that the family has with the company.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Recently, there have been calls to better support employees' mental well-being at workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Anthea Ong asked whether sick leave entitlements can be used for both physical and mental health conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, in issuing a medical certificate, a doctor should not indicate to the employer the nature of the patient's medical condition unless the patient has consented to it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: All employers are expected to practise fair and merit-based employment practices, as laid out in the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For certain jobs, such as pilots and Police Officers, some mental health conditions may affect their ability to perform their job roles effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In these cases, it is reasonable for employers to ask applicants for more information to make a holistic assessment of overall well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Otherwise, employers should not be asking for information on the applicant's mental health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our recent enhanced penalty framework for discriminatory practices also applies to discrimination on grounds of a person's mental health condition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We agree with Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Anthea Ong that employers have an important role in supporting employees' mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, the Ministry of Defence and MOE already have well-developed programmes to support their servicemen and educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We encourage more employers to do the same because your workforce of tomorrow and workforce of today have gone through that system and, as they come out into the workforce, they need the same level of support, too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some employers may want to support their employee's mental health, but they do not know how.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The TA will highlight notable initiatives that companies should emulate, what Mr Melvin Yong was asking for.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These could include progressive practices, such as providing access to anonymised external counselling service or training supervisors, to identify mental health symptoms early.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also work with the tripartite partners and seek views from various stakeholders, including members of the newly announced Youth Mental Well-Being Network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Anthea Ong suggested including mental health expenses as part of employees' medical benefits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Ministry is also happy to partner the Labour Movement to initiate mental health studies and support employee mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For instance, together, we can promote the use of iWorkHealth, a web-based psycho-social assessment tool to help employers and their employees identify workplace stressors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The tool raises awareness of workplace factors that may cause excessive stress and recommends ways to improve mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MOM is currently piloting the tool and will launch it later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked about medical insurance for Work Permit holders (WPHs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Foreign workers who sustain injuries from workplace accidents are entitled to claim compensation under the WICA Framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The compensation cap of $45,000 for medical expenses will fully cover the medical expenses incurred in more than 95% of claims where hospitalisation was required.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To meet WICA obligations, employers are required to purchase WIC Insurance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is separate from the mandatory medical insurance that employers are required to purchase and maintain under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under EFMA, the medical insurance purchase can be used to either supplement the WIC insurance or be used for non-work injury related treatment; so, they are both different.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must always treat all workers fairly and inclusively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As the saying goes, "treat others how you want to be treated".

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is especially important today as we face the COVID-19 threat together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As shared last week, MOM is working hard to educate our foreign workers on the COVID-19 situation and the control measures that we have put in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Materials, such as posters and videos, have been produced and are available in the workers' native languages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In addition, MOM has been sharing bite-size information through our foreign worker ambassadors on a daily basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: An employer from a trading company gave feedback that the handling of the COVID-19 situation was efficient and effective.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One worker shared that he "felt no panic about COVID-19" and that the "Government took a lot of steps against COVID-19".

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But this would not have been possible without our partners – our employers, our unions and our non-government organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We really thank everyone for making this successful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In pursuing inclusive growth in a culture of care for all workers, the Government is committed to ensuring fairness for both employers and workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We can achieve this with the commitment and support of our tripartite partners and fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: By working together hand in hand, we can build the workforce which provides fair support to all employers and workers in an inclusive, empathetic and caring manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to recap how we provide fair and inclusive support to employers and workers in Malay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   MOM will continue to champion fairness and provide fair support for both employers and workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the years, the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) has provided progressive wages and job progression pathways for lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Between 2013 and 2018, wages grew cumulatively by 30% or more for full-time resident workers in these sectors, higher than the 16% for median full-time resident workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Earlier this year, we appointed a tripartite cluster to include escalator technicians under the lift PWM announced in 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will submit its recommendations by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We intend to extend PWM to more sectors, including those where we may not be able to apply mandatory PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will share more when the economic climate is more favourable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also helped lower-wage workers upgrade their skills through the Workfare Training Support Scheme (WTS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since 2010, it has supported over 12,000 companies and 270,000 lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: WTS will be replaced with a new Workfare Skills Support Scheme (WSS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our study of WTS outcomes show that those who train and acquire full qualifications benefit from earning higher wages as a result.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The new WSS will provide higher incentives and training allowances to support workers to achieve full qualifications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together, with the support of the tripartite partners and fellow Singaporeans, we will be able to achieve this goal.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman – long hours, shifting responsibilities, minimal feedback, constant multi-tasking and zero training.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: If you saw a job description like this, would you not run in the opposite direction?

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: And yet, many women take on the important job of caregiving without any pay to speak of.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Caregiving for young children, elderly parents or family members with special needs is often a labour of love.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: But it translates into brutal costs to women's employability, career advancement, income and retirement savings.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Career portal Mums@Work, founded by mumpreneur Sher-li Torrey, supports 43,000 women starting businesses or seeking flexi-work.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Data from their 2019 recruitment campaigns demonstrate the talent of back-to-work females.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Despite these strengths, women face structural, organisational and individual factors that obstruct their return to the workforce.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: One salient structural factor is the achievement orientation in our education system.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In other countries, women tend to take time out from work right after childbirth and, therefore, reintegrate into work when younger.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, they are relatively older when they return to work, thus facing the double whammy of outmoded skills and ageism.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Organisationally, industry feedback indicates that even when companies are prepared to welcome back-to-work women, direct hiring managers still prefer women without career gaps.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: They believe returning women are out of touch with the industry, less dedicated due to their family commitments or cannot gel with younger co-workers.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Even in companies with flexi-work arrangements (FWAs), individual departments may not adopt them or employees themselves may not request them because of the stigma towards flexi-work.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Such prejudices are due to managers not knowing how to manage back-to-work or flexi-work employees.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: We should, therefore, provide more managerial training to address such organisational issues.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Also, we should develop toolkits to help managers onboard and reintegrate returning workers.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Flexi-work and back-to-work hire support schemes are also currently pitched as offering support to individual employees.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: There must be more strategic higher-level communication about the benefits that such hiring shifts can bring to the company to influence individual managers' decision making.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: With the threat of COVID-19, we are currently conducting the greatest telecommuting experiment of all time.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I urge MOM to systematically survey employers and employees to understand the potential and pitfalls of telecommuting.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: We can then identify creative flexi-work solutions and introduce best practices for different industries.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: We should also consider raising SkillsFuture funding for returning women.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Due to their longer career gaps, such women have to write resumes, field interviews and job hunt very differently.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, their upskilling has to be more comprehensive and targeted to their particular needs.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Those who are planning to return to the workforce will still be juggling caregiving with upskilling.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Consequently, they may not be able to attend daylong SkillsFuture courses.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Such factors must be taken into consideration in the design and development of SkillsFuture courses to more effectively support these women.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: This suggests that about half the women did not re-enter the workforce after fulfilling their primary childcare responsibilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I believe we need to do more for our would-be working mothers in the two aspects of exiting and re-entering the workforce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: First, we should try to minimise the disincentives and maximise the incentives for working mothers to remain in the workforce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Besides FWAs, TAFEP and MOM should take proactive steps to clamp down on practices reflecting "motherhood bias", where women are marked as poor performers for juggling family responsibilities while fulfilling their work commitments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Second, the Government is in a good position to help mothers to retrain and update their new skills and reintegrate them into the workforce, especially through various SkillsFuture programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I believe a targeted programme for unemployed mothers would be very useful in this respect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The Government could also support community efforts and partner initiatives, such as Mums@Work, to encourage mothers to remain working and to return to work.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: One explanation for the gap is the inequality in the division of caregiving responsibilities between genders, which significantly limits the choices and opportunities for women.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The need to juggle work and care often results in women ending up in lower-paying jobs which offer more flexible or shorter working hours.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: To tackle this, we can reconfigure workplace culture and enable men to share more equally in caregiving.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: First, the uptake of paternity and shared parental leave by fathers needs to increase.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Reports have found that men who take time off for childcare directly contribute to their female partners' earnings later on in life.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore could consider introducing a compulsory quota for men or offer a longer quantum of gender-neutral parental leave for parents to share as they wish.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Second, work arrangements can be designed to accommodate caregiving.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Employees should have the right to request for FWA.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: A study on the implementation of FWA found that the organisational cultures of workplaces in Singapore did not normalise or formalise FWA.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Employers were also "wary" about the change in facetime with employees under FWA, which could "potentially complicate employee assessment and surveillance".

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Legislating the right for employees to request for FWA could institute an organisational cultural shift.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Work hours in Singapore could also be shorter.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Shorter workhours have also been associated with increased productivity and lower stress levels, according to numerous trials around the world.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: An overall reduction of work time could allow workers to juggle work and care better.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The Ministry can also introduce a dedicated "returnship" programme that provides clear employment pathways for women who wish to return to the labour force.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, the Ministry can also pay more attention to wage levels in female-dominated industries and occupations.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: In a short span of time, many organisations have found themselves willingly or unwillingly implementing FWAs for a sizable proportion of their workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Until recently, for many organisations in Singapore, FWA was a way for employers to allow employees who required it, some flexibility of where and when they work.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: With the current COVID-19 situation, the activation of BCPs involves employees across different roles and levels in the organisation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Moving to FWAs requires not only people to work away from the office, but the right tools, processes and even etiquette or work norms had to be established.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Some companies and employees moved quite quickly while others are still adjusting.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Regardless, we now have quite a large number of organisations and employees on FWAs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I believe that with many employees now experiencing FWAs across their organisations, this will influence and change how people work in the future.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Technology is a key component to enabling new work arrangements and changing how work is done.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: This goes beyond just FWAs to include even shared work and collaborative work spaces.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: With devices getting smarter, connectivity more seamless, the workplace is no longer a place to get work done.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: It is now more important that you have the right devices, access to information and connectivity to get your work done.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: While this will change business norms, it does create new opportunities for both businesses and workers.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: With the competitive labour market, these new work arrangements may become a staff attraction and retention tool for businesses.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I believe that the discussion will move away from flexible work and work-life balance to one of how the boundaries are blurring between work and life as we manage the transformation of how work is done.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Shared or collaborative work arrangements provide platforms for sharing of ideas, creativity and even innovation for companies.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Implementing more flexible and collaborative work arrangements will also require managers to pick up new skills.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Flexi-work provisions, arrangement and support have been extensively rolled out during this COVID-19 outbreak period.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Employees are placed on rotating teams, or being asked to work remotely or from home, while face-to-face meetings are replaced by e-meetings or e-consultations.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Even with some initial inconveniences, we are able to work remotely, flexibly and still fulfil our daily work responsibilities, or even meet our daily business targets, with some creative provisions and solutions in place.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I have spoken about the need to support flexi-work for employees for some time.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: With the current COVID-19 situation, we are somewhat forced to carry out flexi-work provisions and arrangements.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I hope flexi-work can be a common feature of our employment landscape and ecosystem even after COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Just as we trust our workers and staﬀ to work remotely or on a FWA during this period, we must continue to trust them to give the same amount of commitment, time and eﬀort when the worst is over.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Flexi-work is not just for times of crisis or diﬃculty.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Flexi-work is also to allow for personal obligations and commitments to be fulfilled, and to cater to diﬀerent work arrangements and work needs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: For instance, they can work a few days a week in the oﬃce and a few days from home so that they can still work full-time, fulfil their work obligations but can reduce commuting time and yet have the opportunity to meet with colleagues and interact with them face-to-face in the oﬃce for that much needed social interaction.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: For individuals with family commitments and obligations, flexi-work can accord them some much needed time to fulfil these commitments and obligations while they work from home or work remotely, while still ensuring work is done and key performance indicators (KPIs) are met.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I hope the Ministry will continue to provide the needed support and provisions for flexi-work to continue to be implemented by employers.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
text: With such arrangements, through rethinking the work day or redesign of job functions, employers would in all likelihood find it easier to attract and retain locals and reduce reliance on foreign labour.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
text: Today, we find an increasingly diverse workforce – seniors who would like to remain in the workforce, fathers who take on an active role in parenting, for example.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
text: The workforce is no longer homogenous and, as employers, our company policies should respond to such diversity with flexibility.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
text: There are various existing incentives to encourage employers to implement such arrangements in their workplaces.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
text: In the current situation with COVID-19, there is a more compelling reason than before for employers to test out and implement some of the FWAs.

speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
text: This is a window of opportunity that I see here.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: The provision of flexible arrangements has a huge impact on staff retention, as the new generation of workers values flexibility a lot more.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: With COVID-19, many companies have adopted the split-team arrangement, where an alternate team is now stationed at home to support the company's operations.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: This creates an opportunity for companies to assess and try out FWAs and review internal workflows.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
text: As of now, the burden of informal elder caregiving falls disproportionately on unmarried women.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
text: Our dependence on this group of Singaporeans is real, is substantial and very often unacknowledged.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
text: Eldercare leave and the statutory right to FWAs could well help relieve some of the pressures on informal elder caregivers who also work at other jobs.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
text: But almost half of our informal caregivers to seniors do not work at other jobs, often because of the unpaid caregiving responsibilities that they have taken on, to their own financial detriment and to their own reduced retirement adequacy.
