speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, you can do both your cuts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When it comes to work-life balance, Singapore ranks poorly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We rank 32nd out of 40 cities for work-life balance and are second only to Tokyo in a ranking for the most overworked cities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Beyond FWAs, I hope we can also look into increasing the minimum amount of annual leave one is entitled to.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We can have FWAs and still give our people more leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many other countries in this region provide a higher minimum number of annual leave, including Malaysia, Bangladesh, Japan, Myanmar, East Timor, Sri Lanka, Laos, Mongolia, South Korea, Qatar, Yemen, Iran, Kuwait and Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of these countries provide not only a higher number of minimum days of annual leave, but also a higher number of paid public holidays.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our people will always work hard, but we also need to make sure they have time to rest.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Government recognises that we need to spend time looking after our parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been eight years since we introduced parent care leave in the Civil Service and it is now time for everyone else to have this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Time to spend time with our parents runs out quickly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With a rapidly greying population, time is running out for our Government to act on this, too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the Government feels that it is important for civil servants to have parent care leave, then why not others?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are a family-friendly employer and now we need be a family-friendly Government.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
text: Chairman, employers should ensure a safe and inclusive workplace for all workers, regardless of contractual status, by preventing and responsibly handling workplace sexual harassment.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
text: Yet, for many Singaporeans, this unwelcome dilemma is a daily reality.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
text: Many women seeking help from the Workplace Harassment and Discriminatory Advisory at AWARE hesitated at raising a formal complaint with their employers or any other authorities because they did not think that they will be taken seriously.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
text: Some worried that there will be no follow-up action to hold their employers accountable.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
text: These concerns are usually the result of a lack of proper internal structures for reporting and handling harassment complaints.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Josephine Teo and Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad have spoken much on fair opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Earlier on, Members have been given a brochure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is good to highlight the brochure again.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Whatever was covered in the earlier speeches have been very well encapsulated in this very colourful brochure, from providing fair opportunities to ensuring fair hiring, to ensuring fair competition and providing fair support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I also want to add on and say that MOM is also striving to improve work opportunities and progress for our women – many Members have advocated very passionately about that – as well as for caregivers, and also enhance the hiring process of FDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Women in Singapore have made remarkable progress in terms of education, employment and earnings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With improvements in employment rate and education profile, the share of women has risen across broad occupational groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More women are in PMET jobs, rising from 49% to 57% of women over the decade.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will build on the progress achieved to make our workplaces fairer and even more progressive for women.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many women juggle multiple roles, like many hon Members have said earlier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many women juggle multiple roles at work and also at home, juggling our work, family aspirations and also personal aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As women tend to be primary caregivers for families, some may stop work to better care for their families, for their ageing parents, parents-in-law, even aunties and uncles, or for their young children or children with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Prof Lim Sun Sun spoke very passionately and asked about the support for mothers to transition back to work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In this respect, the Government helps in many ways, from matching mothers with options to full-time work with FWAs or part-time work, to providing greater access to childcare support, and promoting FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise that women who have left the workforce for longer periods of time may need additional help, additional support to find jobs, including part-time work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Adapt and Grow initiative offers employment facilitation services and also reskilling as well as professional conversion programmes to help jobseekers enter and transit into new jobs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of these programmes is Career Trial, which provides opportunities for jobseekers and also employers to try each other out over a period of time and assess the job fit – the suitability to the job and also the suitability of the employer to the job, and also whether can the employee work with the people in the organisation and the employer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During the trial, which can be up to three months, jobseekers receive a training allowance from the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, in May 2019, Career Trial was expanded to include part-time jobs to cater for those who prefer part-time work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: There are currently over 500 part-time vacancies available for our Career Trial.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage caregivers to step forward if they are keen to try out part-time positions while balancing their family or balancing their caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Back-to-work women who need career assistance can visit WSG's Careers Connect and NTUC's e2i career centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, as Minister Josephine Teo highlighted last week, during the Prime Minister's Office's (PMO's) COS debate, mothers can now enroll their children in affordable and also good quality preschools more easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We share Ms Yip Pin Xiu's view that childcare is a shared responsibility between the mum and the dad – between both parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The recent increase in shared parental leave supports this, and we hope that the move towards more FWAs will enable fathers as well as mothers to share caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, as our population greys and as the world of work evolves, we have made continual progress to improve our employees’ access to FWAs, not just for women but for all workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Older workers can benefit as they would want to adjust their intensity when they reach a certain age when the grandchildren come along.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, all workers – men and women, young and old – can benefit from FWA, like what Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Jessica Tan rightly mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So far, the Work-Life Grant’s take-up rate has been promising.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And four in five of these companies are SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That means 80% of the Work-Life Grant recipients are SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage more companies, especially our SMEs, or even micro-enterprises to step forward and benefit from this Work-Life Grant to put in place FWAs in their workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More importantly, companies that have put in place FWAs have been better positioned to implement FWAs very quickly, especially in a time of crisis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Like many Members have said earlier, when COVID-19 emerged in January, companies that have already adopted FWAs earlier, already had or could quickly put in place measures, whether it is flexi-time, flexi-place, flexi-load, telecommuting, staggered hours or shared job functions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They could quickly put that in place and this allowed them to minimise disruptions to their business as well as to minimise the team's exposure to the virus.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, I want to assure Miss Cheng Li Hui and also Assoc Prof Daniel Goh and Mr Douglas Foo that more companies are now realising the value and also expediency that FWAs can bring to their employees and also their operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: FWA can be a win-win for the companies and also the employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, this company Kone Private Limited, which is a lift and escalator maintenance company, they have a "flexi-place" arrangement which allows their employees to telecommute and the company could continue their business operations without affecting the productivity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Even prior to the COVID-19 outbreak, its Senior Sales Engineer, Ms Jasmine Tan, who is a mother of two young children, was already enjoying the ease of juggling her work and her family needs through telecommuting, and this has improved her work productivity, as well as job satisfaction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Earlier on, Members talked about the importance of telecommuting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Prof Lim Sun Sun that MOM will continue to monitor such data.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to monitor it as FWAs have proven to be useful for both employers and employees, especially in BCP when threats like COVID-19 strike.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Companies like Kone that I have mentioned earlier, which had FWAs in place before COVID-19, realised that they are much better placed to respond to the crisis and could safeguard their business functions and continuity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, Mr Chairman, FWAs are not simply HR measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In fact, when implemented well, FWAs have the power to enhance the companies’ agility and ability to meet changes and to address business needs as well as to attract and retain talent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope that during this COVID-19 episode, more companies will adopt FWAs and recognise the advantages that such arrangements bring to their business and also their employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat pointed out, every effort to ride out this storm makes a difference because when we combine and aggregate everyone's effort, we have a force that is amplified many times over.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And we are certain that FWAs have already begun to make a positive impact in such a time as this, and the mindset and attitudes of employers towards FWA adoption will gain greater traction and also resonance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Employers are already recognising that FWAs are beneficial to their business.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I think everyone would have read the two-page coverage in The Straits Times on Sunday.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The employers tell us that FWAs have the greatest positive impact on staff retention and recruitment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar will be pleased to know that more employers than before are offering FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together, with enlightened employers and employees, we are confident that we will emerge stronger from this COVID-19 episode.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Singaporeans have given a resounding support to improving access and availability of FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM is committed to doing even more to promote adoption and access to FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Minister Josephine Teo had highlighted in her recent COS speech, the Citizens' Panel, as part of the SG Together movement which was launched by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat, gave strong support to strengthening work-life harmony (WLH) in Singapore, and recognised the important role that FWAs play in this respect.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This Citizens' Panel, comprising 55 Singaporeans from all walks of life, recommended a greater push for FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They had exchanged diverse views and weighed the tradeoffs before putting together their comprehensive report.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Once again, Minister Josephine Teo, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faishal Ibrahim and I would like to say a big thank you to this Citizens' Panel of 55 Singaporeans who came together over four full weekends from September all the way to November to deliberate about this important issue of WLH.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government, NTUC and the Singapore National Employers' Federation (SNEF) greatly appreciate their feedback and are in total agreement to intensify our efforts to spur the adoption of FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: There are four parts to this "Make It Easy" pillar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The first one: some sectors have unique characteristics which will lead to challenges in adopting FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, we all know employees in hospitality and healthcare sectors are required to work shifts, and may not have access to FWAs or even access to staggered hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We acknowledge these hurdles, and we will develop sector-specific resources to facilitate the implementation of FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Jessica Tan earlier had asked about how businesses may leverage new trends and transform their HR practices to encourage greater participation in the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Indeed, there are companies and businesses that are at the forefront of such progressive practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The HR professionals and senior managers from companies that have made FWAs work well for them can share their best practices with the fellow professionals in the sector or even across different sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The third one – under "Make It Easy", we will make it easier for companies to access the myriad of resources on FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, we will revamp TAFEP’s website to be the one-stop resource for everything to do with FWAs, for instance, consolidating all implementation guides so as to make it easy for the companies to adopt.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Those four modes come under "Make It Easy".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The second one, we will "Make It Known" by raising awareness of FWAs – not just FWAs but also WLH initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: HCDT helps companies to better understand their current HR processes better and identify areas for improvement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, this could include appropriate job sizing that is necessary for WLH.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Next, we will also raise awareness on FWAs and the benefits of WLH initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To this end, TAFEP has started to grow a community of Work-Life Ambassadors to spread the word within and beyond the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are grateful to the Labour Members of Parliament and also to the Secretary-General of NTUC and we know they will continue to support union workers as they actively advocate and promote WLH, and also appreciation to SNEF for encouraging employers to appoint champions for WLH.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition to that, we will expand our recognition of employers who are committed to WLH.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, employers who have just started on their FWA journey, it can be quite daunting because they do not quite know where to start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Those of them who have not yet fully adopted the Tripartite Standard on FWAs, for this group of employers we want to "Make It Easy" for them and "Make It Known".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, we will introduce a basic FWA workshop.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This workshop will teach our employers how to start offering FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have now three types: one is the Provisional Tripartite Standard on FWA and the current existing Tripartite Standard on FWA and, for the more progressive, we have the Tripartite Standard on Work-Life Harmony.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, a stepped approach for companies of varying preparedness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Now, within the report are other suggestions considered by the Panel, such as the right-to-request for reduced hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: FWA legislation was also an aspect that was brought up by Ms Anthea Ong and Mr Chen Show Mao.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Though made with good intention, such legislation may lead to unintended consequences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, it could lead to unintended impact of making it unattractive for employers to consider employing those who are likely to exercise the right, such as jobseekers who are caregivers, parents or seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These are told to us by the Citizens' Panel that they would prefer that we have a broad-based adoption of FWAs instead of legislation because they know that legislation is not the silver bullet to solve this issue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And that is why a more practical approach is to provide the employers' support and the flexibility of various types of FWAs which they can choose from that best suit theirs as well as their employees’ needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To sum up, Mr Chairman, we are already working to implement, over the next 12 months, the recommendations which I had just highlighted. "Make It Easy"; "Make It Known".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And the "Make It Easy"; "Make It Known" complement the "Make It Accepted" move that was announced by Minister Josephine Teo last week during the PMO COS debate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Now, with this, we are confident that this collective move for FWAs by the Citizens’ Panel and our tripartite partners will help to make FWAs the norm and also make positive shifts in our workplace culture, like what Ms Jessica Tan has described, and, with that, to further improve WLH in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao had enquired about paid eldercare leave and Mr Louis Ng asked about legislating parent care leave.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure both Members that the needs of working Singaporeans who are also caregivers are utmost on our minds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2018, Senior Minister of State for the Ministry of Health Edwin Tong led an across-agency review, which I am also part of, to better understand the caregivers' need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Compared to family care leave, the working caregivers interviewed, they similarly had the same conclusion as the Citizens' Panel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They felt that FWAs are a more sustainable and preferred means to meet their caregiving needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Because they told us they preferred to have the flexibility and the ability to take some time off when their parents need to go to hospital for appointments or their special needs kids need to go for the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) intervention and so on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They would rather have the flexibility and ability to take some time off when the need arises, rather than have a few more days of leave.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   To overcome the challenges posed by an ageing population and job changes, MOM has been promoting FWAs over the years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will allow more employees to look after their families while working and achieve WLH, which can improve employee loyalty and productivity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will adopt the two-pronged approach that I mentioned previously, which is to "make it easy" and "make it known", so that our businesses can implement FWAs in a sustainable and efficient manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we have to ensure ease of adoption to enable businesses to adopt FWAs easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we must do more to promote FWAs, to create greater awareness of the benefits of FWAs amongst businesses and employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Following the COVID-19 outbreak, many enterprises now agree that this kind of flexible arrangement is beneficial and is a win-win solution for both employers and employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through the strategies of "make it easy", "make it known", we want to enable businesses to adopt FWA easily and effectively, so that more employers will come on board to retain their employees and co-create a sustainable future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, as MOM continually strives to improve working conditions for Singapore workers, we need to make it a point to enhance processes to address workplace harassment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We agree with Ms Yip Pin Xiu that employers play an important role in managing workplace harassment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to assure her and the House that, firstly, TAFEP guides our employers to put in place proper grievance handling process through resources like the TA on managing workplace harassment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So far, all employers that TAFEP has engaged with have been cooperative and receptive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last, not but least, Mr Chairman, allow me to briefly touch on how MOM is improving the employment of FDWs in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM had announced a series of measures in October last year to enable better matches between our employers and FDWs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are rolling out these measures progressively over the next two years to allow all parties to adjust to the changes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is in the interest of both parties to have a lasting employment relationship – employers want minimal disruption to their households and FDWs want a stable income to support their families back home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During the second quarter of this year, MOM will launch an enhanced online Employment Agency (EA) directory to boost the employers' FDW search and give the employers greater clarity in their selection of EAs for their hiring needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides showing the EAs' FDW retention rates, this directory will also feature several other enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, find out the EA's ability to match a suitable FDW and whether past clients would recommend the EA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is important because this will enable prospective employers to more easily compare service offerings from the different EAs and identify one that fits their hiring needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, the improved directory will enable EAs to showcase their niche services, such as providing FDWs trained in caregiving skills, or FDWs who can be swiftly deployed under the Advance Placement Scheme (APS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, Mr Chairman, with greater transparency of information, prospective employers can now make better informed decisions, as well as differentiate the EAs based on their policies and also their performance and track record, thereby improving the chance of a more suitable FDW match.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are strongly encouraging the employers to use the online EA directory to assess and search for a suitable EA before engaging one to hire an FDW.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These enhancements are a result of close consultations with employers through focused group discussions and also the EAs, as MOM seeks to improve the search experience for employers, while enabling the EAs to profile themselves fairly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM will be providing a briefing to EAs on the new features of this enhanced directory to help them adjust to the changes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, we know that getting a good match at the hiring stage is not enough.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To build and maintain a healthy and strong working relationship between employers and FDWs, the employers and FDWs have to be understanding to each other.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And they have also to be fair in their everyday interactions with each other.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To help the first-time FDWs and employers adjust to their new roles, MOM requires them to attend the FDW Settling-in Programme (SIP) and the Employers' Orientation Programme (EOP) respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the SIP, we encourage the FDWs to maintain open communication with the employers and to perform their work duties responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the EOP, we inform the employers of their legal obligations to help them understand their FDWs' culture differences and also encourage the employers to look out for the needs of their helpers, especially in the initial period of employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition to these initiatives, MOM continually works with different stakeholders to support both FDWs and employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, much has been done to support our Singapore workforce – from FWAs to safeguarding employees from unfair treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have also made efforts to developing lasting work relationships between employers and FDWs by enhancing the hiring process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, there is still more that we can do.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Despite the challenges we face today, I believe that our continued efforts will enable us to emerge even stronger.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through the joint efforts of Singaporeans, from employers to employees, from businesses to Government and the tripartite partners and also supporting organisations, everyone plays a part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As long as we are determined to transform, collaborate and work together, we can enhance our workplace and shape a better future together.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Mr Chairman, I filed two cuts earlier, one asking for a review of the Trade Unions Act and the other on the review of Industrial Relations Act and I hope to get a response from the Minister.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, we regularly review the Industrial Relations Act as well as the Trade Unions Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During that time, we will take into consideration the suggestions that the Member has made.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to the Trade Unions Act, in specific, the Member had asked about representation for SEPs, membership and representation for SEPs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, there are already associations that represent them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think if we engage these associations and hear them out, we could probably find a way forward that they would also be comfortable with.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: I made a cut on the electronic salary payment for WPHs.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Could the Minister of State tell us the proportion of WPHs who are already paid electronically and whether MOM will consider making e-payment of salary for WPHs mandatory?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Chairman, our laws today already require employers and WPH to provide e-salary payment if the workers request for it.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, we know we work together with MWC to educate workers as well as share with them their rights so that they can also go to the employers and request for these.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, MWC has been conducting SIPs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, during these programmes, it will help workers who wish to be paid electronically.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time as well, we also know through talking to stakeholders that there are micro SMEs that have expressed concerns, the mom-and-pop shops, for example, which have difficulties in the short term.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I think the numbers will go up in the long term.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, let us study this and see how best we can bridge the gap.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Chairman, I thank Minister of State Mr Zaqy Mohamad for sharing the good news on workplace mental health today.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I think my mental health definitely got better after his speech.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Given that there is still stigma that exists in the workplace on mental health, it is really quite difficult for persons with mental health conditions to ask for FWAs.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I appreciate Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling saying that it is not going to be working in our favour to legislate the right to FWAs.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: But can I ask if the Citizens' Panel, which recommended that, had any persons with mental health conditions on the Panel?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: If not, would the Ministry and the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling consider the specific needs of persons with mental health conditions as we embark on all the wonderful efforts on FWAs, going forward?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Ms Anthea Ong.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As she started off, I thought the clarification was directed at the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And then, I think it got boomerang back.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But I want to thank her for her passion in this area.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier on, I did not have the time but allow me to share this.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Two years ago, I was involved in Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong's cross-agency committee for caregivers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And that Motion was tabled in February 2019.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Last year, in September, Minister Josephine Teo sponsored the Citizens' Panel on WLH.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Interestingly, both committees came to the same conclusion on their own.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the caregiving committee, they interviewed many caregivers, not just caregivers with aged parents but also caregivers with younger children.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They also came up with the original wish list of legislating the right to request for FWA, legislating more leave and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, the Citizens' Panel came to their conclusion that legislation cannot be a silver bullet for every issue.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They recognised that whether it is FWAs or WLH, everyone has a role to play.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And, with that, they shared with us that it is important, in order to achieve broad-based adoption of FWA and then, eventually, WLH, including for persons with mental wellness issues, the important thing is to encourage adoption of FWAs and also greater awareness.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That is why in the past few months, we have been working with them to see how we can distil into very tangible items under "Make It Easy", "Make It Known" and "Make It Accepted".

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, one of the interesting things they discussed during their sessions was the right to request for FWA that has been introduced in some countries, such as the UK, New Zealand, Canada and Australia.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But we have found that in these countries, such legislation, although passed, merely gives the employees the right to ask for FWA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Interestingly, there have been anecdotal evidence saying that the employers can still reject the FWA applications based on a wide range of reasons that seem very reasonable and valid.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, UK employers have rejected FWA applications on the grounds of additional costs or how it could affect the quality of work.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Citizens Panel is rightly concerned that if we look at legislation as a way to address this issue, it may lead to the unintended impact of eroding the employability for the very people we are trying to protect and whom we are trying to make sure will benefit from FWA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: A lot of the response to my suggestions so far has been that we will focus on FWA instead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I think we need to acknowledge that FWA is not going to be accessible to everyone, as the Senior Parliamentary Secretary has acknowledged just now, especially to our frontline officers whom we have been paying tribute to over the last few weeks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It will be very hard for nurses, doctors, teachers, preschool teachers, cleaners, security – the list goes on – to have access to FWA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And that is why I say it is not a zero-sum game.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We are doing this for the Civil Service already.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I do not think it was responded to.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I have a stronger focus on that because I think the workers who get the seven days of annual leave, which is the minimum number, are likely to be our lowest-income workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And they are also the workers who probably need the most rest.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I appreciate Mr Louis Ng's passion in advocating for more leave provisions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In an ideal world, I would like to be able to say yes to all of them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we do not live in an ideal world.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I am very much reminded by our former Minister for Labour Mr S Rajaratnam when he moved the Employment Act in 1968.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He reminded us of why we are here and why we are seeking to improve work conditions through the Employment Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He was responding to many Members' calls for employer obligations in many different areas – more protection in this area, more protection in another area.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, the jobs must be available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If there is no employment, there is no employment protection to speak of.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, for every of the moves that MOM tries to make, it is always in consultation, not only with the Labour Movement whom we can completely count on to speak up on behalf of workers and to try and advocate for their interests, but at the same time, we must also involve the employers in this conversation and hear them out and understand the pressures that they face, and then make a judgement call at different times, what kinds of pressures we are prepared to exert in order to get the best outcomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we are the true sandwich class, in some sense.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But let us keep all these things in mind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I see no reason why we cannot continue to review our policies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I believe that, at the right time, when conditions allow, we would certainly want to improve the employment conditions for all of our workers.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I cannot help but chip into the discussion on FWA even though I did not speak, if I may.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I think this is something that we have in the People's Action Party (PAP) Women's Wing been championing.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: We have always talked it from the legislation angle and how everybody wants it.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Actually, a lot of research has already been established to say this is good for business.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Businesses which do it have lower turnover, higher performance, morale is good, higher job satisfaction – all the good things.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Perhaps one approach if MOM can take a lead is to evangelise the benefits of FWA with employers, so that it is something that they will embrace by being a great place to work, so that they can attract the best talent.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I think perhaps that is something that we all have agreement.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: And I think it is proven that it is good for business.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, if we can look at that, that would be great.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Mr Chairman, I want to thank Member Ms Foo Mee Har and also the Women's Wing Members of Parliament for advocating for this FWA issue very passionately over the course of a few years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is important that we continue to "evangelise", a word the Member used.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Minister Josephine Teo, Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad and myself have, for the past two years, been doing that with the TACs, including the Singapore Business Federation and SNEF.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: One important thing we learnt – and I think this is what Ms Foo Mee Har is alluding to and links to the first move that I mentioned – is coming up with and developing sector-specific resources.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the past, we had a very generic TA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We realised that for some sectors, they have certain constraints, especially with work shifts and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It could come in the form of a guide.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And that will come about because we have a discussion with the sector and also with some companies in the sector that are more progressive and have been put in place FWA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will then crystalise that into a guide or even video, which then makes it easier for them to share within a company and with other companies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Chairman, earlier, I filed the cut on the existing Special Employment Credit (SEC).

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: I would just like to clarify with the Minister, where older PMETs are concerned, how effective has the existing SEC been at job retention versus facilitating hiring.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: I am asking because retention may well be easier than hiring retrenched PMETs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: So, how will the Ministry approach these challenges separately with the redesign of the SEC and the renewed emphasis on supporting senior employment?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, a number of schemes work in concert with one another to support senior employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Truth be said, we do not depend solely on SEC and what is to replace the SEC.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Their feedback to us was that there have been occasions where they would like their senior workers to go for training and to be ready to be redeployed into different positions when they come to re-employment, so that the positions that they occupied could be freed up to also younger colleagues to move up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Sometimes, it is just a lack of motivation to take up training.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Sometimes, from the workers' standpoint, he thinks, "Well, if I am not going to be in work for very much longer, why ask me to go for training?" Hence, we were able to persuade the employers that if they gave the workers the assurance, even PMETs, that they have a longer runway, then perhaps this could motivate them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are very grateful to the Labour Movement for being very involved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Company Training Committees can really exert an influence on the ground.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Peer support – everyone going to train at the same time, everyone in their 50s, 60s and learning data analytics, everyone trying digitalisation tools.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We cannot depend on laws alone, we cannot depend on guidelines alone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I promise the Minister this is the last time I will talk about leave provisions this week.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I just ask whether MOM has studied or will be studying whether increasing someone's annual leave entitlement will reduce employability?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A whole host of factors come into play.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A well-timed move of the same change may not have that impact.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Having said that, let me reassure Mr Louis Ng, whether it is this week or next week, it will always be on MOM's mind to think of ways in which we can improve work conditions as well as WLH.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Patrick Tay, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I am sure all the measures that the Minister and the team have announced to be fairer, be it in terms of fair support, fair hiring, fair opportunities as well as fair competition, will help us, namely, workers, employers and the various tripartite partners in all the respective sectors, to stay ready, relevant and resilient to the short-term disruptions; and able, agile and adaptable to the long-term challenges.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: On that note, I would like to beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
